title: Beyond the Cross-Encoder: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Beyond the Cross-Encoder: Visual Guide

1. The Interaction Spectrum | three tappable architecture cards - bi-encoder, late interaction, cross-encoder - recomputing encoder runs, dot products, bytes stored per document and whether the document side ever sees the query, against a candidates-per-query slider | late interaction is the engineered midpoint: the interaction is deferred rather than compressed, so precomputation survives while token-level evidence is kept

2. MaxSim Token By Token | the worked example - query `visa required for layover` against a transit-visa page and a long-stay visa page, five tappable query-token rows showing which document token won each max, and a slider on the one similarity that separates them | the score is max over the document then sum over the query, so every query token must be answered somewhere and one unanswered token decides the ranking at the 0.88 crossover

3. The Token Vector Bill | a tokens-per-document slider and a corpus-size selector feeding a four-step PLAID stepper, showing index size, documents touched, exact MaxSim scorings and dot products falling at each cut | keeping every token costs 30-50x a single vector, and PLAID's three cuts - centroid compression, centroid pruning, residual refinement - are the lesson-01 ranking funnel rebuilt inside one model

4. Teacher And Student | three modes over one distillation example - shift and scale sliders showing margin-MSE is shift-invariant while pointwise MSE is not, a soft-label slider on the plausible negative, and a queries-per-day and rerank-depth pair costing the two ledgers | the student learns the teacher's score gaps rather than its scale, soft scores carry the near-miss information hard labels destroy, and the teacher's bill is fixed and offline while the student's is recurring and online
